actors_note: The red is people's choices: site operators chose to publish machine-written articles with little or no human oversight to collect programmatic ad money. threat.notes: extent = count / 3,749 (latest count). Doubling times derived here from the points: early 49 -> 600 over 7.49 months = 2.1 months per doubling (49 -> 217 in the first 1.84 months was faster still, 0.86 months, but that stretch is mostly NewsGuard finding existing sites, not new ones appearing); late 1,121 -> 3,006 over 15.96 months = 11.2 months per doubling; whole run 49 -> 3,006 = 5.8 months. CAVEATS: these are one organization's detections, not a census; early growth is partly detection effort; the definition changed from 'Unreliable AI-generated News sites' to 'AI Content Farm' sites and from Mar 2026 detection is partly automated, which can raise counts. Use as a lower bound on growth, and say 'counted' not 'exist'.

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented dates, not a measured distribution: p10 = the funders are told their ads are on these sites (Jun 2023, t=1.84, s3); median = search spam policy targeting scaled content (Mar 5, 2024, t=10.15, s9); p90 = a real-time detection feed offered to platforms and advertisers (Mar 12, 2026, t=34.36, s7). No source found on whether the 141 brands pulled ads, or when.

deploy.notes: Search policy announced Mar 5, 2024 and rollout complete Apr 19, 2024 (45 days = 1.48 months), with a reported 45% cut in low-quality unoriginal results. The site count still grew from ~700 to 3,006 after it: the fix reduced reach in one channel, not creation.

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative, and partly real: the pieces for AI used well already exist here and were joined in Mar 2026 (s7: automated detector plus human reviewers). Counterfactual: the same detection-plus-review loop is connected to ad buyers and search at the first count instead of after ~34 months. Classifying every newly registered 'news' domain is a short, repetitive task well inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry), and RATES.md's ~40x/yr fall in cost at fixed capability (Epoch) is what makes screening every new site affordable. Assumed ~2 months from first count to a routed feed that advertisers and search can act on, versus the human median of ~10 months (first platform policy) and ~34 months (real-time feed). Detectors make mistakes, so humans still review and decide what to defund or demote. Does not assume the sites stop being made.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: Counted junk AI news sites went 49 -> ~600 in 7.5 months (doubling every ~2 months); the first platform policy came at ~10 months and a real-time detection feed at ~34, by which time the count was 3,006 and still doubling about yearly.
